problem.title: Scaling the Transactional Outbox with CDC
problem.prompt: Your payment ledger writes 15,000 transactions/sec into PostgreSQL 16, inserting one row into `outbox_events` per transaction. Eight relay workers poll `outbox_events` every 50ms using `SELECT ... WHERE status = 'PENDING' ORDER BY id LIMIT 500 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and then `UPDATE status = 'SENT'` (or `DELETE`). Within 4 hours of peak load, `outbox_events` bloats from 200 MB to 48 GB despite holding only 50,000 pending rows, autovacuum lags behind due to long-running analytics queries, polling p99 jumps from 8ms to 1,400ms, and Kafka lag exceeds 400,000 events. Redesign the outbox ingestion and relay pipeline to sustain 20,000+ events/sec with < 50ms end-to-end publish latency and zero table bloat.

spark.summary: Under 15,000+ writes/sec, polling a PostgreSQL transactional outbox table with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and `DELETE`/`UPDATE` generates massive MVCC dead tuples, starves autovacuum, bloats B-tree indexes, and stalls event relay.
spark.keyTakeaway: Replace SQL polling on high-throughput outbox tables with PostgreSQL WAL Logical Replication (Debezium `pgoutput`), or pair time-partitioned outbox tables with `DROP`/`TRUNCATE` rotation to eliminate MVCC bloat.

learningJourney.explanation: Writing payment ledger rows and `outbox_events` in one ACID transaction eliminates dual-write bugs. However, when 8 relay workers poll `outbox_events` every `50 ms` using `SELECT ... WHERE status = 'PENDING' LIMIT 500 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` followed by `UPDATE status = 'SENT'` (or `DELETE`) at `15,000–20,000 writes/sec`, PostgreSQL's MVCC engine collapses within 4 hours.

learningJourney.title: Dead-tuple explosion, autovacuum starvation, and bloated B-trees
learningJourney.explanation:
PostgreSQL MVCC never overwrites rows in place—every `UPDATE` or `DELETE` creates dead tuples:

1. **2x Dead-Tuple Churn**: `15k/s` inserts + `15k/s` updates/deletes generate `30k` tuple versions/sec that cannot be vacuumed while any analytics `xmin` snapshot is open (`15 min`).
2. **Index & Lock Thrashing**: The `status = 'PENDING'` B-tree bloats to gigabytes of dead entries, blowing past `40,000` IOPS.

learningJourney.title: Enterprise solution: Append-Only Partitioned Outbox + Debezium pgoutput
learningJourney.explanation:
Sustain `20,000` outbox inserts/sec with `< 50 ms` p99 Kafka relay lag:

- **Append-Only `outbox_events` (Zero `UPDATE`/`DELETE`)**: Insert events in the same ACID transaction as the ledger, and never update or delete rows.
- **Debezium `pgoutput` WAL Streaming**: Read sequential Write-Ahead Log records directly from the replication slot (zero polling queries, zero lock contention), using `OutboxEventRouter` SMT to partition Kafka by `aggregate_id` for per-aggregate ordering.
- **Hourly Range Partitions + `DROP TABLE`**: Partition `outbox_events` by `created_at` (hourly/daily) and drop expired partitions in `O(1)` metadata time—bypassing `VACUUM` completely.

_nextProblem.title: Tuning Kubernetes HPA for Sudden Traffic Surges
_nextProblem.prompt: A ticketing API runs on Kubernetes (minReplicas=10, maxReplicas=120) with a standard CPU HPA targeting 70% utilization. When a concert ticket drop hits at 10:00:00, RPS jumps 10x (from 2,000 to 20,000 RPS) in 12 seconds. Pods saturate CPU and drop connections within 20 seconds, yet HPA does not trigger scale-up until 10:01:15. New pods then sit in Pending for 110 seconds waiting for Karpenter/Cluster Autoscaler to provision EC2 nodes, plus 35 seconds for JVM warmup and readinessProbe. By the time capacity arrives at 10:03:40 (~3.7 minutes late), 45% of checkout requests have timed out with HTTP 503. Redesign the autoscaling and surge-absorption architecture to handle 10x spikes in < 30 seconds.

_problemQuestions.prompt: A user edits their bio and refreshes the page, only to see the old bio for 2 seconds because the read hit a lagging replica. Which consistency guarantee was violated?

options.explanation: Read-Your-Writes ensures a client always observes its own completed writes.
The write was durable on the primary; the replica simply lagged.
Atomicity governs all-or-nothing commit, not cross-replica visibility.

_problemQuestions.prompt: Why does placing `request_timestamp` at the very beginning of a 3,000-token system prompt hurt latency and cost?

options.explanation: BPE still tokenizes the text normally.

options.text: It invalidates prefix/KV caching for all subsequent 3,000 tokens on every request
options.explanation: Correct! Prefix KV caching requires an exact token match from index 0 onward.
Output length is unaffected; Prefill cache reuse is what breaks.
